item.title: PNJ Taps Chairwoman’s Family for Loan After Diamond Scandal
item.description: Phu Nhuan Jewelry JSC, Vietnam’s largest listed jeweler known as PNJ, is securing a loan from the family of Chairwoman Cao Thi Ngoc Dung to rebuild its business after a national diamond-smuggling scandal battered the industry.

item.title: Ex-RBA Official Expects September Hike, 10% Drop in House Prices
item.description: Australia’s central bank is likely to deliver another interest-rate increase at its meeting later this month, according to a former senior Reserve Bank official, who also expects property prices will fall by about 10%.

item.title: Andreessen-Backed AI Startup Gimlet Is Valued at $3 Billion in New Round
item.description: The company, which helps divide AI tasks among different chips, raised $300 million in its latest round

item.title: India Says US Trade Deal Hinges on Preferential Tariff Rate
item.description: India will finalize a trade deal with the US once Washington offers tariff terms that give exporters an advantage over competitors, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said, signaling a key sticking point in protracted negotiations between the two countries.

item.title: Sharp Price Swings Prompt SEBI Review of India’s Closing Auction
item.description: Regulator may propose changes to the way settlement prices for equity derivatives contracts are calculated.

item.title: Bathla Crisis Puts Focus on $94 Million of Unsecured Debts
item.description: Bathla Group’s administrator gave a breakdown of known creditors for the first time as talks remain ongoing to stave off liquidation at the embattled Sydney property developer.

item.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak: Roche to Expand Testing Capacity in Ituri
item.description: Roche Holding AG plans to deploy new laboratory equipment in the epicenter of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola epidemic as authorities struggle to contain a virus that has repeatedly outrun the response.

item.title: Japan Ministries Seek Larger Budget as Fiscal Concerns Mount
item.description: Japanese ministries requested substantially more spending for next fiscal year, with some major items still unresolved and investors focused on how large the final budget will become, and how the government will pay for it.

item.title: Chinese University of Hong Kong Seeks Loan to Fund Its Hospital
item.description: Chinese University of Hong Kong is seeking a bank loan of around HK$4 billion ($510 million) to refinance a facility supporting its private hospital, according to people familiar with the matter, as local universities increasingly turn to debt financing for major projects.

item.title: Nomura Says Three Straight BOJ Hikes Possible in Extreme Case
item.description: The Bank of Japan could raise interest rates at three consecutive meetings through December in an extreme scenario where yen weakness persists, according to Nomura Securities Co.

item.title: Fading Cobalt Rally Is Testing Congo’s Efforts to Control Prices
item.description: Cobalt’s spectacular rally is reversing as the Democratic Republic of Congo’s exports of the battery metal pick up under a strict new regime, testing the top producer’s efforts to control prices.

item.title: RBNZ More Likely To Wait Until December to Hike, Silk Says
item.description: New Zealand’s central bank is more likely to wait until December before raising interest rates again, according to Assistant Governor Karen Silk.

item.title: Philippine Inflation Eases to 6.1% After Successive Rate Hikes
item.description: Philippine inflation eased for the fourth straight month in August while staying above the central bank’s target, on slower increases in utility rates and food prices.

item.title: Carry Trade Exodus Fuels Yen Surge Ahead of BOJ Rate Decision
item.description: A rush to unwind yen-funded carry trades helped send the currency to a one-month high against the dollar as traders ramped up bets on further Bank of Japan rate hikes.

item.title: SoftBank Group Prices ¥1 Trillion Retail Bond at 4.75%
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. priced a ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) retail bond with a coupon of 4.75%, as higher rates boost the appeal of bonds, potentially drawing more companies to retail funding.

item.title: Pacific Leaders Criticize China’s Recent Missile Test
item.description: The leaders of Pacific island nations took a thinly-veiled swipe at China’s recent missile test in their region, an unexpected move after earlier failed attempts to agree on a response.

item.title: Japan’s Households Cut Outlays for Eighth Month Amid Inflation
item.description: Japanese households cut spending for an eighth consecutive month as rising costs for daily necessities prompt consumers to pare discretionary purchases.

item.title: BOE’s Pill Fears Central Banks Being Pushed to Finance Deficits
item.description: The biggest threat to central banks’ independence comes from governments pushing them to finance huge fiscal deficits, according to the Bank of England’s chief economist.

item.title: Anthropic Finalizing $15 Billion Pre-IPO Credit Facility
item.description: Anthropic PBC is set to finalize an expansion of its revolving credit facility to $15 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, clearing a hurdle before the artificial intelligence firm’s public filing for its highly anticipated IPO.

item.title: Crusoe Raises Over $3 Billion in Funding at $30 Billion Valuation
item.description: Crusoe, a cloud-computing provider and data center developer doing business with OpenAI, Microsoft Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc., has raised over $3 billion in a funding round that values the startup at roughly $30 billion, according to people familiar with the situation.

item.title: Asia Stocks to Gain as Fed Bets Cool, Dollar Drops: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were poised to rise Friday, tracking gains on Wall Street as investors pared bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike this month. The yen held its biggest gain in over a month and oil rose.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 4
item.description: Oil headed for its biggest weekly gain since July as renewed US-Iran hostilities heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: India Launches Rocket in Boost to Space Ambitions After Failures
item.description: India’s space program notched a much-needed success with a rocket launch on Friday, after two consecutive failures of another launcher that had long served as its workhorse rocket.

item.title: FBI Investigating Possible Exposure of Millions of American IDs
item.description: The FBI is investigating a potential breach of an ID verification company that may have exposed scans of millions of Americans’ driver’s licenses, a bureau spokesperson told Bloomberg News on Thursday.

item.title: Korea’s Financial Labor Union to Strike Against Relocation Plans
item.description: South Korea’s financial industry union plans to strike to protest the government’s push to relocate public institutions out of Seoul, escalating opposition to President Lee Jae Myung’s drive to spread economic activity beyond the capital.

item.title: Anthropic Executive Doesn’t Want to ‘Buy Market Share’ With Price Cuts
item.description: The Claude maker is competing with more affordable options from rivals

item.title: SEC Moves to Nix Rule on Adviser Political Donations
item.description: Investment advisers would no longer be prohibited from offering services to public pension funds if they made recent political donations to state and local elected officials, the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a proposed rule change Thursday.

item.title: Australia’s Battered Bonds Have Reasons to Rebound, Funds Say
item.description: Australia’s bonds, caught up in the global fixed-income selloff, have seen their yields rise more than any of their peers in the past month, despite arguments that the country’s finances are in much better shape.

item.title: Los Angeles Schools Ban Student Use of AI Tools on District Devices
item.description: The Los Angeles Unified School District is barring students from using generative AI tools on district devices as part of a broader push to reduce screen time in the classroom.

item.title: Meet the Biggest Ad Buyer in the Podcasting Industry
item.description: BetterHelp is the top podcast advertiser of all time. Since 2023, the talk therapy provider has spent $242 million on ads in the space, according to one firm’s estimates
